import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.67

by E. I. Khukhro

An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of prime order $p$*
(see Problem 10.59) if $\varphi^p = 1$ and
$x x^{\varphi} x^{\varphi^2} \cdots x^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $x \in G$; the identity
automorphism of a group of exponent $p$ is allowed. Such groups are regarded as groups with
one operator $\varphi$. The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ of locally nilpotent groups admitting a
splitting automorphism of prime order $p$ is a variety of groups with operators
(E. I. Khukhro, *Math. USSR Sbornik* **58** (1987), 119–126). Is it true that
$$LN\mathfrak{M}_p = (\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)} \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p) \vee
(\mathfrak{B}_p \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p),$$
where $\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)}$ is the variety of nilpotent groups of some $p$-bounded class $c(p)$
and $\mathfrak{B}_p$ is the variety of groups of exponent $p$?

Here $\vee$ is the join in the lattice of varieties of groups with operators, i.e. the smallest
variety of groups with one operator containing both classes.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

universe u

namespace Kourovka.«10.67»

/-- An automorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of order $p$* if
$\varphi^p = 1$ and $x x^{\varphi} x^{\varphi^2} \cdots x^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all
$x \in G$. The identity automorphism of a group of exponent $p$ is allowed. -/
def IsSplittingAutomorphism {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) (φ : MulAut G) : Prop :=
  φ ^ p = 1 ∧ ∀ x : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (φ ^ i) x).prod = 1

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if all its finitely generated subgroups are nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group with one operator: a group `carrier` together with an automorphism `op`
of `carrier`. -/
structure OperatorGroup : Type (u + 1) where
  /-- The underlying group. -/
  carrier : Type u
  [group : Group carrier]
  /-- The operator. -/
  op : MulAut carrier

attribute [instance] OperatorGroup.group

/-- A class `𝒱` of groups with one operator is a *variety* if it is closed under homomorphic
images (in particular quotients by operator-invariant normal subgroups and isomorphic copies),
operator-invariant subgroups, and Cartesian products with the operator acting componentwise.
Homomorphisms here are group homomorphisms commuting with the operators. -/
structure IsVariety (𝒱 : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop where
  /-- `𝒱` is closed under homomorphic images. -/
  image : ∀ (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) (f : A.carrier →* B.carrier), Function.Surjective f →
    (∀ x, f (A.op x) = B.op (f x)) → A ∈ 𝒱 → B ∈ 𝒱
  /-- `𝒱` is closed under subgroups. -/
  sub : ∀ (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) (f : B.carrier →* A.carrier), Function.Injective f →
    (∀ x, f (B.op x) = A.op (f x)) → A ∈ 𝒱 → B ∈ 𝒱
  /-- `𝒱` is closed under Cartesian products. -/
  prod : ∀ (ι : Type u) (A : ι → OperatorGroup.{u}), (∀ i, A i ∈ 𝒱) →
    OperatorGroup.mk (∀ i, (A i).carrier) (MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i => (A i).op) ∈ 𝒱

/-- The variety of groups with one operator generated by a class `𝒮`: the smallest variety
containing `𝒮`, i.e. the intersection of all varieties containing `𝒮`. -/
def varietyClosure (𝒮 : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  ⋂₀ {𝒱 | IsVariety 𝒱 ∧ 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒱}

/-- The join $\mathcal{A} \vee \mathcal{B}$ of two classes of groups with one operator in the
lattice of varieties: the smallest variety containing both. -/
def varietyJoin (𝒜 ℬ : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  varietyClosure (𝒜 ∪ ℬ)

/-- The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ of locally nilpotent groups with a splitting automorphism of
order $p$, regarded as groups with one operator. -/
def locallyNilpotentSplitting (p : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | IsLocallyNilpotent A.carrier ∧ IsSplittingAutomorphism p A.op}

/-- The class $\mathfrak{N}_c$ of groups with one operator whose underlying group is nilpotent of
class at most $c$. -/
def nilpotentOfClassLE (c : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | lowerCentralSeries A.carrier c = ⊥}

/-- The class $\mathfrak{B}_p$ of groups with one operator whose underlying group has exponent
dividing $p$, i.e. satisfies the law $x^p = 1$. -/
def burnside (p : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | ∀ x : A.carrier, x ^ p = 1}

/-- The identity automorphism is a splitting automorphism of order `p` exactly on groups
satisfying the law $x^p = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplittingAutomorphism_one_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) :
    IsSplittingAutomorphism p (1 : MulAut G) ↔ ∀ x : G, x ^ p = 1 := by
  simp [IsSplittingAutomorphism, List.map_const', List.prod_replicate]

/-- For $p = 3$, $\varphi$ is a splitting automorphism of order $3$ if and only if
$\varphi^3 = 1$ and $x x^{\varphi} x^{\varphi^2} = 1$ for all $x$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplittingAutomorphism_three_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] (φ : MulAut G) :
    IsSplittingAutomorphism 3 φ ↔ φ ^ 3 = 1 ∧ ∀ x : G, x * φ x * φ (φ x) = 1 := by
  simp [IsSplittingAutomorphism, List.range_succ, pow_succ, MulAut.mul_apply, mul_assoc]

/-- The variety generated by a class is a variety. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isVariety_varietyClosure (𝒮 : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) :
    IsVariety (varietyClosure 𝒮) where
  image A B f hf hop hA := Set.mem_sInter.2 fun 𝒱 h𝒱 =>
    h𝒱.1.image A B f hf hop (Set.mem_sInter.1 hA 𝒱 h𝒱)
  sub A B f hf hop hA := Set.mem_sInter.2 fun 𝒱 h𝒱 =>
    h𝒱.1.sub A B f hf hop (Set.mem_sInter.1 hA 𝒱 h𝒱)
  prod ι A hA := Set.mem_sInter.2 fun 𝒱 h𝒱 =>
    h𝒱.1.prod ι A fun i => Set.mem_sInter.1 (hA i) 𝒱 h𝒱

/-- A class is contained in the variety it generates. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem subset_varietyClosure (𝒮 : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) : 𝒮 ⊆ varietyClosure 𝒮 :=
  fun _ hA => Set.mem_sInter.2 fun _ h𝒱 => h𝒱.2 hA

/-- The variety generated by a class is the smallest variety containing it. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem varietyClosure_subset {𝒮 𝒱 : Set OperatorGroup.{u}} (h𝒱 : IsVariety 𝒱) (h : 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒱) :
    varietyClosure 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒱 :=
  fun _ hA => Set.mem_sInter.1 hA 𝒱 ⟨h𝒱, h⟩

/--
Let $p$ be a prime. The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ of locally nilpotent groups admitting a
splitting automorphism of prime order $p$ (an automorphism $\varphi$ with $\varphi^p = 1$ and
$x x^{\varphi} \cdots x^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $x$; the identity automorphism is allowed),
regarded as groups with one operator, is a variety of groups with operators. Is it true that
$$LN\mathfrak{M}_p = (\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)} \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p) \vee
(\mathfrak{B}_p \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p),$$
where $\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)}$ is the variety of nilpotent groups of some $p$-bounded class $c(p)$
and $\mathfrak{B}_p$ is the variety of groups of exponent $p$?

Here $\vee$ is the join in the lattice of varieties of groups with operators, and "$p$-bounded"
means that $c(p)$ depends only on $p$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.67» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ c : ℕ,
      locallyNilpotentSplitting.{0} p =
        varietyJoin (nilpotentOfClassLE c ∩ locallyNilpotentSplitting p)
          (burnside p ∩ locallyNilpotentSplitting p) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.67»

The table's reading (single yes/no question, implicit ∀ prime p and ∃ c depending only on p, objects are groups with an operator φ that is a splitting automorphism of order p with the identity allowed, ∨ the join in the lattice of varieties of groups with operators, opening sentence a cited fact) matches the statement and Khukhro's definitions, and the file follows it.
modeling_decisions: The operator φ is modelled as `MulAut G` (an automorphism) rather than a general endomorphism `G →* G`. In the variety M_p the law φ^p = 1 forces every operator (and every operator on subalgebras, quotients, products) to be an automorphism, so the join of two subclasses of LN M_p is the same in the lattice of varieties of groups with an automorphism operator and in the lattice of varieties of groups with one endomorphism operator.

A variety (`IsVariety`) is a class closed under (i) operator-preserving surjective homomorphic images — this covers quotients by operator-invariant normal subgroups and isomorphic copies —, (ii) operator-preserving injective homomorphisms (operator-invariant subgroups up to isomorphism), (iii) Cartesian products `∀ i, G i` with the componentwise operator `MulEquiv.piCongrRight`. The join is defined abstractly as `⋂₀ {𝒱 | IsVariety 𝒱 ∧ 𝒜 ∪ ℬ ⊆ 𝒱}` (the smallest variety containing both), matching the lattice join literally rather than via the HS(A × B) description.

The theorem is stated with carriers in `Type` (universe 0), i.e. classes are `Set OperatorGroup.{0}` and the join is the smallest universe-0 variety. By Birkhoff's theorem the universe-0-relative join agrees with the true join restricted to groups in `Type`, so this is not a restriction; the auxiliary definitions themselves are universe polymorphic.

The equality of classes is stated literally (both inclusions). The inclusion ⊇ is exactly Khukhro's cited theorem that LN M_p is a variety (closed under H, S, P); the open content is ⊆. The cited theorem is described in the docstrings but not stated as a separate declaration, since the decomposition table treats it as background.

"p-bounded class c(p)" is rendered as `∃ c : ℕ` after `∀ p, p.Prime →`, i.e. c depends only on p. N_c is "nilpotent of class ≤ c" (`lowerCentralSeries G c = ⊥`), and B_p is the Burnside variety given by the law x^p = 1 (so the trivial group belongs to it), rather than `Monoid.exponent G = p`.
`IsLocallyNilpotent G` is defined as `∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H`.

The order of the product x·x^φ·…·x^{φ^{p-1}} is the standard increasing order; unit tests `isSplittingAutomorphism_one_iff` (φ = 1 ⇔ law x^p = 1) and `isSplittingAutomorphism_three_iff` (p = 3 unfolds to φ^3 = 1 ∧ x·φx·φ(φx) = 1) check the definition.

All bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (as the task requires a single file); a reviewer may prefer moving `OperatorGroup`, `IsVariety`, `varietyClosure`, `varietyJoin`, `IsSplittingAutomorphism`, `IsLocallyNilpotent` to `FormalConjecturesForMathlib`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.67

by E. I. Khukhro

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.67
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.67»

universe u

/-- A group with one distinguished operator, represented by an automorphism. -/
structure OperatorGroup where
  carrier : Type u
  group : Group carrier
  operator : MulAut carrier

attribute [instance] OperatorGroup.group

/-- A homomorphism of groups with operators is a group homomorphism that commutes with the
specified operators. -/
structure OperatorGroup.Hom (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) where
  toMonoidHom : A.carrier →* B.carrier
  map_operator : ∀ x, toMonoidHom (A.operator x) = B.operator (toMonoidHom x)

instance {A B : OperatorGroup.{u}} : CoeFun (OperatorGroup.Hom A B)
    (fun _ ↦ A.carrier → B.carrier) :=
  ⟨fun f ↦ f.toMonoidHom⟩

/-- The Cartesian product of a family of groups with operators, with the operator acting
coordinatewise. -/
def OperatorGroup.pi {ι : Type u} (A : ι → OperatorGroup.{u}) : OperatorGroup.{u} where
  carrier := ∀ i, (A i).carrier
  group := Pi.group
  operator := MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ (A i).operator

/-- A class of groups with operators is a variety if it is closed under operator-preserving
subgroups, operator-preserving quotients, and Cartesian products. The injective and surjective
homomorphism formulations include closure under operator-preserving isomorphisms. -/
def IsOperatorGroupVariety (V : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ {A B}, V A → ∀ f : OperatorGroup.Hom B A, Function.Injective f → V B) ∧
  (∀ {A B}, V A → ∀ f : OperatorGroup.Hom A B, Function.Surjective f → V B) ∧
  (∀ {ι : Type u} (A : ι → OperatorGroup.{u}), (∀ i, V (A i)) → V (OperatorGroup.pi A))

/-- The join of two classes in the lattice of varieties of groups with operators: the smallest
variety containing both classes. -/
def operatorVarietyJoin (V W : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop) : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop :=
  fun A ↦ ∀ U, IsOperatorGroupVariety U → (∀ B, V B → U B) → (∀ B, W B → U B) → U A

/-- The underlying group is locally nilpotent if each of its finitely generated subgroups is
nilpotent. -/
def OperatorGroup.IsLocallyNilpotent (A : OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup A.carrier, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- The distinguished automorphism is a splitting automorphism of order dividing `p`: its
`p`th power is the identity and
$x\,\varphi(x)\cdots\varphi^{p-1}(x)=1$ for every $x$. In accordance with Problem 10.59,
the identity automorphism is allowed. -/
def OperatorGroup.HasSplittingOperator (p : ℕ) (A : OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  A.operator ^ p = 1 ∧
    ∀ x : A.carrier, ((List.range p).map fun i ↦ (A.operator ^ i) x).prod = 1

/-- The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ of locally nilpotent groups with a specified splitting
automorphism of order dividing $p$. -/
def locallyNilpotentSplittingClass (p : ℕ) : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop :=
  fun A ↦ A.IsLocallyNilpotent ∧ A.HasSplittingOperator p

/-- The variety $\mathfrak{N}_c$ of groups nilpotent of class at most $c$, equipped with an
arbitrary distinguished automorphism. -/
def nilpotentClassAtMost (c : ℕ) : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop :=
  fun A ↦ lowerCentralSeries A.carrier c = ⊥

/-- The variety $\mathfrak{B}_p$ of groups satisfying the identity $x^p=1$, equipped with an
arbitrary distinguished automorphism. -/
def exponentDividingClass (p : ℕ) : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop :=
  fun A ↦ ∀ x : A.carrier, x ^ p = 1

/--
For every prime $p$, is there a bound $c(p)$ depending only on $p$ such that
$$
LN\mathfrak{M}_p =
  (\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)} \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p) \vee
  (\mathfrak{B}_p \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p),
$$
where the join is the join of varieties of groups with the distinguished operator (closure under
operator-preserving subgroups, quotients, and Cartesian products),
$\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)}$ consists of groups nilpotent of class at most $c(p)$, and
$\mathfrak{B}_p$ consists of groups of exponent dividing $p$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.67» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ c : ℕ,
      locallyNilpotentSplittingClass p =
        operatorVarietyJoin
          (fun A ↦ nilpotentClassAtMost c A ∧ locallyNilpotentSplittingClass p A)
          (fun A ↦ exponentDividingClass p A ∧ locallyNilpotentSplittingClass p A) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.67»
modeling_decisions: A group with operators is modeled as a group equipped with one distinguished automorphism, matching the single splitting operator in Problems 10.59 and 10.67.

The phrase “order p, identity allowed” is modeled by φ^p = 1. Since p is prime, this permits precisely order p or the identity; the splitting identity is stated separately using an ordered List product because the group need not be commutative.

A variety of operator groups is modeled by closure under injective operator homomorphisms (subgroups up to operator-preserving isomorphism), surjective operator homomorphisms (quotients up to operator-preserving isomorphism), and arbitrary same-universe Cartesian products. The join is the intersection of all such varieties containing both classes.
Local nilpotence means that every finitely generated subgroup of the underlying group is nilpotent; the subgroup need not be invariant under the distinguished operator.

The class N_c is expressed by lowerCentralSeries G c = ⊥, which means nilpotency class at most c under Mathlib's indexing. The class B_p is expressed by the identity x^p = 1, i.e. exponent dividing p; this is the standard variety called the variety of groups of exponent p and correctly includes the trivial group.
The existential c occurs after the universally quantified prime p and before equality of whole classes, so c depends only on p and is uniform across all operator groups.
The opening cited assertion that LN M_p is itself a variety is treated as background, not as a second conjecture declaration.

  group : Group carrier

/-- A homomorphism of groups with operators is a group homomorphism commuting with the
operators. -/
structure OperatorGroup.Hom (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) extends A.carrier →* B.carrier where
  map_operator : ∀ x, toMonoidHom (A.operator x) = B.operator (toMonoidHom x)

  coe f := f.toMonoidHom
  coe_injective' f g h := by cases f; cases g; simp_all

coordinatewise. -/
def pi {ι : Type u} (A : ι → OperatorGroup.{u}) : OperatorGroup.{u} where
  carrier := ∀ i, (A i).carrier
  group := inferInstance
  operator := MulEquiv.piCongrRight fun i ↦ (A i).operator

end OperatorGroup

/-- A class of groups with operators is a variety if it is closed under equivariant subgroups,
equivariant quotients, and Cartesian products. -/
structure IsOperatorGroupVariety (C : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop) : Prop where
  subgroup : ∀ {A B}, C B → (f : OperatorGroup.Hom A B) → Function.Injective f → C A
  quotient : ∀ {A B}, C A → (f : OperatorGroup.Hom A B) → Function.Surjective f → C B

/-- The join of two classes of groups with operators: the smallest variety containing both. -/
def varietyJoin (C D : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop) : OperatorGroup.{u} → Prop :=

* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 10.67
* E. I. Khukhro, *Locally nilpotent groups that admit a splitting automorphism of prime order*,
  Math. USSR Sbornik **58** (1987), 119–126,
  [doi:10.1070/SM1987v058n01ABEH003095](https://doi.org/10.1070/SM1987v058n01ABEH003095)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.67»

/-- A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- An endomorphism $\varphi$ of a group $G$ is a *splitting automorphism of order $p$* if
$\varphi^p = 1$ (so $\varphi$ is in fact an automorphism) and
$x \, x^{\varphi} \, x^{\varphi^2} \cdots x^{\varphi^{p-1}} = 1$ for all $x \in G$.
The identity is allowed: it is splitting of order $p$ exactly when $x^p = 1$ for all $x$. -/
def IsSplittingOfOrder {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) (φ : G →* G) : Prop :=
  (∀ x : G, (⇑φ)^[p] x = x) ∧ ∀ x : G, ((List.range p).map fun i => (⇑φ)^[i] x).prod = 1

/-- A *group with operator*: a group together with a fixed endomorphism, the operator. -/
structure OperatorGroup : Type 1 where
  /-- The underlying type. -/
  carrier : Type
  /-- The group structure. -/
  [instGroup : Group carrier]
  /-- The operator. -/
  op : carrier →* carrier

attribute [instance] OperatorGroup.instGroup

/-- The Cartesian product of a family of groups with operators, with the operator acting
componentwise. -/
def OperatorGroup.pi {ι : Type} (X : ι → OperatorGroup) : OperatorGroup where
  carrier := ∀ i, (X i).carrier
  op := Pi.monoidHom fun i => (X i).op.comp (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun i => (X i).carrier) i)

/-- A class `𝒱` of groups with operators is a *variety* if it is closed under
operator-invariant subgroups, operator-compatible quotients and Cartesian products
(equivalently, by Birkhoff's theorem, if it is defined by a set of laws in the signature of
groups with one unary operator). -/
structure IsVariety (𝒱 : Set OperatorGroup) : Prop where
  /-- Closure under subobjects: if `f : Y → X` is an injective group homomorphism intertwining
  the operators and `X ∈ 𝒱`, then `Y ∈ 𝒱`. -/
  mem_of_injective : ∀ (X Y : OperatorGroup) (f : Y.carrier →* X.carrier),
    Function.Injective f → f.comp Y.op = X.op.comp f →
    X ∈ 𝒱 → Y ∈ 𝒱
  /-- Closure under quotients: if `f : X → Y` is a surjective group homomorphism intertwining
  the operators and `X ∈ 𝒱`, then `Y ∈ 𝒱`. -/
  mem_of_surjective : ∀ (X Y : OperatorGroup) (f : X.carrier →* Y.carrier),
    Function.Surjective f → f.comp X.op = Y.op.comp f →
    X ∈ 𝒱 → Y ∈ 𝒱
  /-- Closure under Cartesian products. -/
  pi_mem : ∀ (ι : Type) (X : ι → OperatorGroup), (∀ i, X i ∈ 𝒱) → OperatorGroup.pi X ∈ 𝒱

/-- The join `𝒦₁ ∨ 𝒦₂` of two classes of groups with operators in the lattice of varieties:
the smallest variety containing both `𝒦₁` and `𝒦₂`. -/
def varietyJoin (𝒦₁ 𝒦₂ : Set OperatorGroup) : Set OperatorGroup :=
  ⋂₀ {𝒱 | IsVariety 𝒱 ∧ 𝒦₁ ⊆ 𝒱 ∧ 𝒦₂ ⊆ 𝒱}

/-- The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ of locally nilpotent groups with a splitting automorphism of
order $p$, regarded as a class of groups with operators. -/
def LNM (p : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup :=
  {X | IsLocallyNilpotent X.carrier ∧ IsSplittingOfOrder p X.op}

/-- The variety $\mathfrak{N}_c$ of nilpotent groups of class at most $c$, regarded as a class of
groups with operators (with arbitrary operator). -/
def nilpotentVariety (c : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup :=
  {X | lowerCentralSeries X.carrier c = ⊥}

/-- The Burnside variety $\mathfrak{B}_p$ of groups of exponent $p$, i.e. groups satisfying the
law $x^p = 1$, regarded as a class of groups with operators (with arbitrary operator). -/
def burnsideVariety (p : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup :=
  {X | ∀ x : X.carrier, x ^ p = 1}

/-- The identity operator is a splitting automorphism of order $p$ exactly when the group
satisfies the law $x^p = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSplittingOfOrder_id_iff {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) :
    IsSplittingOfOrder p (MonoidHom.id G) ↔ ∀ x : G, x ^ p = 1 := by
  simp [IsSplittingOfOrder, Function.iterate_id, List.map_const', List.prod_replicate]

/-- The operator on a Cartesian product acts componentwise. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem OperatorGroup.pi_op_apply {ι : Type} (X : ι → OperatorGroup)
    (x : (OperatorGroup.pi X).carrier) (i : ι) :
    (OperatorGroup.pi X).op x i = (X i).op (x i) :=
  rfl

/-- The join of two classes contains both of them. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem subset_varietyJoin_left (𝒦₁ 𝒦₂ : Set OperatorGroup) :
    𝒦₁ ⊆ varietyJoin 𝒦₁ 𝒦₂ :=
  fun _ hX => Set.mem_sInter.2 fun _ h𝒱 => h𝒱.2.1 hX

/-- The join of two classes contains both of them. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem subset_varietyJoin_right (𝒦₁ 𝒦₂ : Set OperatorGroup) :
    𝒦₂ ⊆ varietyJoin 𝒦₁ 𝒦₂ :=
  fun _ hX => Set.mem_sInter.2 fun _ h𝒱 => h𝒱.2.2 hX

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.67

by E. I. Khukhro

The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ consists of locally nilpotent groups equipped with a
splitting automorphism of prime order $p$. It is known to be a variety of groups
with an operator. The problem asks whether this variety is generated by its
members of bounded nilpotency class together with its members of exponent $p$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.67»

universe u

/-- A group with one distinguished automorphism. -/
structure OperatorGroup where
  carrier : Type u
  group : Group carrier
  operator : carrier ≃* carrier

attribute [instance] OperatorGroup.group

/-- A homomorphism of groups with an operator is a group homomorphism commuting
with the distinguished operators. -/
structure OperatorGroup.Hom (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) where
  toMonoidHom : A.carrier →* B.carrier
  map_operator : ∀ x, toMonoidHom (A.operator x) = B.operator (toMonoidHom x)

instance {A B : OperatorGroup.{u}} : CoeFun (OperatorGroup.Hom A B)
    (fun _ ↦ A.carrier → B.carrier) :=
  ⟨fun f ↦ f.toMonoidHom⟩

/-- `A` is an operator-preserving subobject of `B` if there is an injective
operator-preserving homomorphism from `A` to `B`. -/
def IsOperatorSubobject (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : OperatorGroup.Hom A B, Function.Injective f

/-- `B` is an operator-preserving homomorphic image of `A` if there is a
surjective operator-preserving homomorphism from `A` to `B`. -/
def IsOperatorImage (A B : OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : OperatorGroup.Hom A B, Function.Surjective f

/-- `A` is an operator-preserving Cartesian product of the family `F` if it is
isomorphic as a group to the Cartesian product and the isomorphism commutes
with the operators coordinatewise. -/
def IsOperatorProduct {ι : Type u} (A : OperatorGroup.{u})
    (F : ι → OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : A.carrier ≃* ((i : ι) → (F i).carrier),
    ∀ (x : A.carrier) (i : ι), e (A.operator x) i = (F i).operator (e x i)

/-- A variety of groups with one operator, expressed by its closure under
operator-preserving subobjects, homomorphic images, and Cartesian products. -/
def IsOperatorGroupVariety (V : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∀ ⦃A B⦄, V B → IsOperatorSubobject A B → V A) ∧
  (∀ ⦃A B⦄, V A → IsOperatorImage A B → V B) ∧
  (∀ {ι : Type u} (F : ι → OperatorGroup.{u}) ⦃A⦄,
    (∀ i, V (F i)) → IsOperatorProduct A F → V A)

/-- The join of two classes in the lattice of varieties: the least variety
containing both classes. -/
def varietyJoin (C D : Set OperatorGroup.{u}) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | ∀ V, IsOperatorGroupVariety V → C ⊆ V → D ⊆ V → V A}

/-- The distinguished automorphism is splitting of order dividing `p`: its
`p`-th iterate is the identity and every ordered orbit product is one. This
includes the identity automorphism when it satisfies the splitting identity. -/
def HasSplittingOperator (p : ℕ) (A : OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  (∀ x, A.operator^[p] x = x) ∧
  (∀ x, (List.ofFn fun i : Fin p ↦ A.operator^[i.val] x).prod = 1)

/-- A group is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup is
nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (A : OperatorGroup.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set A.carrier, S.Finite → Group.IsNilpotent (Subgroup.closure S)

/-- The class $LN\mathfrak{M}_p$ of locally nilpotent groups with a splitting
operator of order dividing `p`. -/
def LNM (p : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | IsLocallyNilpotent A ∧ HasSplittingOperator p A}

/-- The class of operator groups whose underlying group is nilpotent of class
at most `c`. -/
def nilpotentClassAtMost (c : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | lowerCentralSeries A.carrier c = ⊥}

/-- The class of operator groups whose underlying group has exponent dividing
`p`. -/
def exponentClass (p : ℕ) : Set OperatorGroup.{u} :=
  {A | ∀ x : A.carrier, x ^ p = 1}

/--
For every prime $p$, is there a bound $c(p)$, depending only on $p$, such that
$$
LN\mathfrak{M}_p =
  (\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)} \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p) \vee
  (\mathfrak{B}_p \cap LN\mathfrak{M}_p)?
$$
Here $\mathfrak{N}_{c(p)}$ is the variety of groups nilpotent of class at most
$c(p)$, $\mathfrak{B}_p$ is the variety of groups of exponent $p$, and the join
is taken in the lattice of varieties of groups with the distinguished
operator.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.67» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ c : ℕ,
      LNM p = varietyJoin (nilpotentClassAtMost c ∩ LNM p) (exponentClass p ∩ LNM p) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.67»
modeling_decisions: Groups with operators are bundled as groups equipped with one distinguished multiplicative automorphism; morphisms commute with that automorphism.

A variety is modeled semantically by closure under operator-preserving injective homomorphisms, surjective homomorphisms, and small Cartesian products. The join is the intersection of all such varieties containing both input classes.
The universe-relative product closure quantifies over index types in the carrier universe, the standard small-product interpretation for a class of small operator groups.
Following the decomposition note that the identity is allowed, 'order p' is represented by the operator's p-th iterate being the identity, rather than requiring its exact order to equal p.
The splitting identity uses a List product indexed in the order 0 through p-1, since the underlying group need not be commutative.
Local nilpotence is expressed by nilpotence of the subgroup generated by every finite subset.
Nilpotency class at most c is expressed as the c-th lower central series subgroup being bottom; exponent p is expressed by x^p = 1 for every element.
